newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-MYLLYLAE SAVES BEST FOR LAST.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-MYLLYLAE SAVES BEST FOR LAST.

text.p: Finn Mika Myllylae saved his best for last when he won the final event at the Nordic skiing world championships on Sunday with a stylish victory in the 50-km classic.
Second in the 15-km pursuit and the relay and third in the 10-km classic, the 27-year-old Myllylae has lived in the shadows of local hero Bjorn Daehlie over the previous nine days.
But on Sunday, the powerful Finn tamed the demanding conditions of pouring rain and sticky snow to clock a winning time of two hours 16 minutes 37.50 seconds.

Norway's Erling Jevne earnt his first placing in an individual event at a world championships, finishing 54.90 seconds back in second. A tiring Daehlie had to be content with bronze 1:58.50 behind the winner.
Cheered on by some 40,000 fans who braved miserable weather to come and support their hero, triple gold medallist Daehlie made a strong start and led for some 30 kilometres.
As Daehlie dropped back, Myllylae widened his lead on Jevne in the final three laps of the bumpy circuit.
"The conditions were really tough today and when I woke up this morning and saw what the weather was like, I thought I wouldn't make it," he said.
"I had a new pair of skis which I had never used before and I was afraid about the waxing but in the end, everything was just fine. It's a dream come true."
Daehlie, who won gold over the distance at the 1992 Olympics in Albertville, said the drain of 10 days of competition had taken its toll.
"Those championships have been very successful for me and I'm happy," he said.
"That race, coming at the end of a long competition, is always very difficult. I was tired and in the last 20 kilometres, I just couldn't keep up with Mika."

There was disappointment for Vladimir Smirnov of Kazakhstan, who won three golds at the 1995 world championships in Thunder Bay, Canada, after he finished 19th in Sunday's race to leave Trondheim empty handed.
